Viktor.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first early on, and choose Mercury’s Treads. Viktor’s damage is mostly magic, and Irelia has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize building magic resistance.
Viktor.fight: Before trading, hit minions with abilities to stack Irelia P Ionian Fervor. Lock Viktor down with Irelia E Flawless Duet from outside Viktor W Gravity Field, then engage. Viktor has no dash to escape on his own, so close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge after landing the stun.
Viktor.laning: Rather than forcing an engage on ranged Viktor, secure CS by finishing low-health minions with Irelia Q Bladesurge to keep its reset available. Don’t stand in line with the minions so Viktor E Hextech Ray can’t hit you and the wave together. Check minion positions for engaging and retreating, and don’t force your way in and waste Irelia E Flawless Duet.
Viktor.combo: Then dash in with Irelia Q Bladesurge, land basic attacks, and use Irelia W Defiant Dance. Hit the marked target with Irelia Q Bladesurge to reset its cooldown, and plan your next path so you don’t remain inside Viktor W Gravity Field.
Viktor.escape: Look for an opening to engage when Viktor W Gravity Field is on cooldown or you’ve moved outside its area. Viktor has no dash, so stun Viktor with Irelia E Flawless Duet and close in with Irelia Q Bladesurge. Keep in mind that Viktor Q Siphon Power increases Viktor’s movement speed, which can create distance.
Viktor.phase: Viktor P Glorious Evolution’s growth stacks are permanent, so it’s best to pressure Viktor early, before any augments. Once Viktor has accumulated augments in the mid game or later, reassess the trade even if the opening looks the same as before.
Viktor.teamfight: After your allies land crowd control, use Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge to block Viktor’s escape route and split the enemy formation. Lock down the trapped target with Irelia E Flawless Duet, then dive in with a chain of Irelia Q Bladesurge casts. Don’t keep attacking inside Viktor W Gravity Field; leave its area to avoid the stun.

Volibear.watch: When Volibear activates Volibear Q Thundering Smash and approaches, its empowered attack can stun you, so stay outside his attack range and wait it out. When you see the marker for Volibear E Sky Splitter, walk to the side to avoid the damage and slow, and watch where Volibear is trying to gain a shield. Don’t take a fight while Volibear builds stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm as he approaches.
Volibear.build: Build armor first to prepare for the damage from Volibear Q Thundering Smash, Volibear W Frenzied Maul, and Volibear R Stormbringer. If Volibear W Frenzied Maul’s healing keeps negating your short trades, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Volibear E Sky Splitter deals damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about choosing items that only add a lot of health.
Volibear.fight: Build stacks of Irelia P Ionian Fervor by hitting minions with abilities, then use Irelia Q Bladesurge to dash to a minion you can finish and take a short trade. Save Irelia E Flawless Duet to stun Volibear when he retaliates or retreats. If you can’t finish him while Volibear W Frenzied Maul can heal him, back off and wait out its cooldown.
Volibear.laning: Use Irelia Q Bladesurge on minions you can finish to reset its cooldown, and leave a minion to escape to. When you see the marker for Volibear E Sky Splitter, walk out of its area and look for the direction of your next engage.
Volibear.combo: Follow up with basic attacks and Irelia W Defiant Dance. You can use Irelia Q Bladesurge again after its cooldown resets from Irelia E Flawless Duet’s mark to stick to him.
Volibear.escape: Look to engage after Volibear Q Thundering Smash is down, but check whether Volibear can still use Volibear R Stormbringer. In particular, before Volibear R Stormbringer comes back up, it’s hard for him to escape if you close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge and stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet. When Volibear Q Thundering Smash chases you, look for a minion to use Irelia Q Bladesurge on and reset its cooldown instead of running in a straight line.
Volibear.phase: At any stage, avoid fighting while Volibear has stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm, and look to engage as soon as they fall off.
Volibear.teamfight: After an ally lands crowd control, use Irelia R Vanguard's Edge to split the formation and escape routes on Volibear’s side, then lock down a target with Irelia E Flawless Duet and chain in with Irelia Q Bladesurge. If Volibear R Stormbringer is available, don’t stay under your turret at low health; retreat farther back to safety. If he telegraphs his leap, look for a minion you can use Irelia Q Bladesurge on to move away from the landing spot.

Xerath.watch: If Xerath E Shocking Orb stuns you, you can take his full follow-up, so prioritize dodging that shot. Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so move well to the side when you see him charging it. Watch out for the slow from Xerath W Eye of Destruction, and start dodging as soon as you see the cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Xerath.build: Build Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Xerath’s primary damage is magic, so build magic resistance before armor.
Xerath.fight: Close the gap right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Approach by using Irelia Q Bladesurge to finish low-health minions, then start a trade by stunning him with Irelia E Flawless Duet. Before going in, build stacks of Irelia P Ionian Fervor by hitting minions with abilities.
Xerath.laning: Rather than forcing your way onto ranged Xerath, farm only minions you can finish with Irelia Q Bladesurge and scale. Xerath Q Arcanopulse can hit you even behind minions, so move to the side when you see him charging it. Farm while avoiding heavy damage, then push the lane and call your jungler when Xerath runs low on mana.
Xerath.combo: Follow up with a dash using Irelia Q Bladesurge, basic attacks, and Irelia W Defiant Dance. Irelia Q Bladesurge’s cooldown resets when it hits Xerath marked by Irelia E Flawless Duet, letting you stick to him with consecutive dashes.
Xerath.escape: Xerath has no mobility, so the moment after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down is your window to engage. Close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge and lock him down with Irelia E Flawless Duet.
Xerath.phase: You grow stronger as you complete more items in the mid and late game, but avoid dying by forcing bad engages.
Xerath.teamfight: After an ally lands crowd control, use Irelia R Vanguard's Edge to split the area around Xerath’s team. Lock down a trapped target with Irelia E Flawless Duet, then dive into the backline with a chain of Irelia Q Bladesurge dashes. The cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane can also give you a chance to engage, since Xerath can’t move while casting it.

Zed.watch: Watch where the shadows from Zed W Living Shadow appear, and move outside their range to avoid the slow from Zed E Shadow Slash. When Zed engages with Zed R Death Mark, he’ll try to build up damage until the mark detonates, so stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet to interrupt his combo.
Zed.fight: Build up your passive stacks in advance, then repeat short trades where you engage and back off. Engage after Zed uses Zed W Living Shadow, once the shadow has disappeared or he has already switched places with it, and use Irelia E Flawless Duet to stop Zed from retaliating or escaping.
Zed.laning: Use Irelia Q Bladesurge only on low-health minions you can finish, securing a cooldown reset and an escape route.
Zed.combo: Follow up with a dash using Irelia Q Bladesurge, basic attacks, and Irelia W Defiant Dance.
Zed.escape: Don’t engage just because Zed W Living Shadow alone is down. Before Zed R Death Mark comes back up, wait for a moment when he can’t escape with Zed W Living Shadow either, then close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge and lock him down with Irelia E Flawless Duet.
Zed.phase: Zed peaks in the mid game, so don’t give him an early lead and avoid forcing engages. In the late game, group with your allies so Zed has no isolated target to pick off.
Zed.teamfight: After an ally lands crowd control, use Irelia R Vanguard's Edge to block Zed’s escape route and split the enemy team. Lock down a trapped target with Irelia E Flawless Duet, then dive in with consecutive Irelia Q Bladesurge dashes.
Zed.build: Build armor early since most of the damage from Zed Q Razor Shuriken, Zed E Shadow Slash, and Zed R Death Mark is physical. Zed P Contempt for the Weak deals magic damage based on your maximum health, so armor can’t block it; avoid choices that only add a lot of health.

Yone.watch: When Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions to prepare his tornado, stay out of range and wait for the stacks to fall off. When he engages with Yone E Soul Unbound, he can deal extra damage as he returns, so use Irelia Q Bladesurge’s healing before your health gets low or create distance. Yone R Fate Sealed pulls in enemies along its path, so don’t stand alone at the very back of your team in a team fight.
Yone.build: Build movement speed first so you can get out of the way of Yone’s telegraphed attack areas. Yone deals a mix of physical and magic damage, so don’t focus all your resistance on one type. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on your maximum health, so be wary of choices that only add a lot of health.
Yone.fight: Build stacks of Irelia P Ionian Fervor by hitting minions with abilities, then take short trades where you engage and back off. If Yone engages with Yone E Soul Unbound, save Irelia E Flawless Duet to stun him, delay his return, and retaliate. You can also interrupt Yone’s tornado, Yone Q Mortal Steel, with Irelia E Flawless Duet, but first position yourself to land the stun.
Yone.laning: Use Irelia Q Bladesurge on minions you can finish to reset its cooldown, and leave a minion path for your return.
Yone.combo: When your mark lands, dash in with Irelia Q Bladesurge, basic attack, then follow up with Irelia W Defiant Dance. Use Irelia Q Bladesurge, reset by the mark, either to stick to Yone or to escape to a minion.
Yone.escape: Don’t engage just because Yone Q Mortal Steel alone is down; also check whether he has used Yone E Soul Unbound and Yone R Fate Sealed. In particular, before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back up, close the gap if you have a route through a low-health minion with Irelia Q Bladesurge. Then stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet to stop his escape.
Yone.phase: In the mid to late game, both champions grow stronger with items, so rather than assuming one has the advantage, look for a moment when Yone’s engage tools are down.
Yone.teamfight: After an ally lands crowd control, use Irelia R Vanguard's Edge to split the area around Yone’s team, then follow up with Irelia E Flawless Duet and Irelia Q Bladesurge. Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield doesn’t grow as large, and don’t stand alone at the very back of your team where Yone R Fate Sealed can pull you in. If Yone dives in first, stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet to delay his return with Yone E Soul Unbound.

Yorick.watch: Yorick E Mourning Mist slows, marks, and deals damage based on maximum health, so dodge the orb’s trajectory. Don’t start a fight when many graves have built up or ghouls are on you; clear the ghouls first. If you’re trapped in Yorick W Dark Procession, hit the wall to break it or look for a route over it with Irelia Q Bladesurge.
Yorick.build: Build armor first against Yorick Q Last Rites and the ghouls’ physical damage. Yorick E Mourning Mist and Yorick R Eulogy of the Isles deal damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying on a large health stack alone. If Yorick Q Last Rites healing keeps nullifying your short trades, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
Yorick.fight: Before fighting, hit minions with abilities to build Irelia P Ionian Fervor stacks, then last-hit low-health minions with Irelia Q Bladesurge to create a route. Dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist, trade briefly, and interrupt Yorick with Irelia E Flawless Duet when he retaliates or backs off. Clear the ghouls before approaching Yorick.
Yorick.laning: Don’t fight where many graves have built up near Yorick. Push the lane so minions die under Yorick’s turret, then step forward to farm after Yorick E Mourning Mist misses. Use Irelia Q Bladesurge on minions you can kill to reset it and preserve an escape route.
Yorick.combo: If Yorick retaliates, reduce the damage with Irelia W Defiant Dance.
Yorick.escape: When Yorick E Mourning Mist misses, that’s your chance to engage. If Yorick W Dark Procession is also down, close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge and stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet. Check the position of minions you can finish with Irelia Q Bladesurge in case you need to retreat.
Yorick.teamfight: After your team’s crowd control lands, split the enemy formation with Irelia R Vanguard's Edge. Stun a trapped target with Irelia E Flawless Duet, then chain Irelia Q Bladesurge to dive into the back line. If Yorick is alone pushing a turret in a side lane, consider trading by taking an objective elsewhere.
Yorick.phase: Irelia gets stronger as you build items, but don’t fall to a reckless engage while responding to Yorick’s side-lane pressure.

Zoe.watch: If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble hits you, you’ll fall asleep a moment later, making Zoe Q Paddle Star! easy to land. Dodge the bubble; if it hits, move behind a wall or an ally before sleep triggers to get out of Zoe Q Paddle Star!’s angle and range. When you see Zoe winding up Zoe Q Paddle Star!, stun her with Irelia E Flawless Duet to prevent her from redirecting it.
Zoe.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zoe’s damage is mostly magic, so prioritize magic resistance, but resistance doesn’t reduce the true damage from Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble; focus on dodging the bubble.
Zoe.fight: Just before a fight, hit minions with abilities to build Irelia P Ionian Fervor stacks. Once Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down, close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge on a minion.
Zoe.laning: Against ranged Zoe, safely scale by using Irelia Q Bladesurge to last-hit only low-health minions and reset its cooldown. Check first for minions to use when engaging and retreating, and don’t waste Irelia E Flawless Duet on a forced engage. Watch for the trap left by a missed Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble in narrow paths and at brush entrances without vision.
Zoe.combo: When Zoe R Portal Jump appears, place Irelia E Flawless Duet to catch her where she returns to her starting point.
Zoe.escape: Right after Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down, you have a chance to engage with Irelia Q Bladesurge. Before going in, check the minion positions and leave a route to escape with Irelia Q Bladesurge.
Zoe.phase: From the mid game onward, Irelia gets stronger as she completes more items, but don’t sacrifice your growth with an overforced engage.
Zoe.teamfight: Before an objective, use a Control Ward to light up the area and spot traps from Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble. After your team’s crowd control lands, block Zoe’s escape route with Irelia R Vanguard's Edge, then stun her with Irelia E Flawless Duet and dive in with chained Irelia Q Bladesurge. If Zoe uses Zoe R Portal Jump, target the point where she’ll return.

Yasuo.watch: After Yasuo lands Yasuo Q Steel Tempest twice, his next attack knocks enemies up, so watch for the sound and visual effect and dodge sideways. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade uses minions as stepping stones to approach, so keep an eye on nearby minion positions.
Yasuo.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest and Yasuo R Last Breath. Attack speed reduction also helps slow his basic attacks and the return cycle of his tornado.
Yasuo.fight: Before fighting, hit minions with abilities to build Irelia P Ionian Fervor stacks. Break Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield first, then briefly engage and back off as soon as Yasuo launches Yasuo Q Steel Tempest’s tornado. Save Irelia E Flawless Duet to interrupt Yasuo if he retaliates or runs away.
Yasuo.laning: Manage the wave so a thin wave pushes toward your side to limit the minions Yasuo E Sweeping Blade can use as stepping stones. Use Irelia Q Bladesurge on minions you can kill to reset its cooldown and preserve an escape route. Don’t engage first with Irelia Q Bladesurge on Yasuo when he has no mark.
Yasuo.combo: Then dash in with Irelia Q Bladesurge and land basic attacks before using Irelia W Defiant Dance. You can use the Irelia Q Bladesurge reset from the mark to stick to him again.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo launches the tornado from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest is your chance to engage. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t chase just because he used it once. Before Yasuo R Last Breath is available again, close the gap with Irelia Q Bladesurge and stun him with Irelia E Flawless Duet.
Yasuo.teamfight: After your team’s crowd control lands, split the formation around Yasuo with Irelia R Vanguard's Edge. Stun a trapped target with Irelia E Flawless Duet, then dive in with chained Irelia Q Bladesurge. Before engaging, also check for a route using minions or other targets with Irelia Q Bladesurge.
Yasuo.phase: You get stronger as you build items, but avoid reckless engages that stunt your growth.
